recipes.name: Grandma Jeanette's Amazing German Red Cabbage

steps.text: Place cabbage, apples, sugar, and butter into a large pot. Pour in vinegar and water, then add salt, pepper, and cloves. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer until the cabbage is tender, 1 ½ to 2 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Grandma Jeanette's Amazing German Red Cabbage
raw_recipe.description: This German red cabbage recipe is easy to make with shredded red cabbage, apples, sugar, and cider vinegar for a deliciously sweet and sour side dish.

video.description: The authentic German red cabbage recipe in this video is a uniquely delicious dish with sweet, sour, and delicately spiced flavor. It's a standout side dish that uses pantry staples, shredded red cabbage, and sliced apples to create a vibrantly colored, fork-tender bite you'll never forget.
video.name: How to Make Amazing German Red Cabbage

review.reviewBody: I recently went to dinner at my extended family's home and they served up this dish. It was absolutely fantastic! Admittedly, I enjoy cabbage. Admittedly, I am not big on cloves. But, put together and is terribly tasty. After I found out the recipe was from here I immediately looked it up and was surprised by what little feedback there was. I must say I probably would have skipped this recipe over with so few people having tried it. How great that I was able to have an opportunity to try this keeper of a recipe. It is on my stove as we speak (really) and I am going to cook it just as directed for the full 2 hours. I know first hand it is worth it. I wouldn't change a thing!

I used to get this same red cabbage at alittle resturant inside a cattle sells barn in west , tx. (same town they have the world famous westfest) I have looked everwhere for it and now my life is complete,I did add 1tsp. of carraway seeds to give it a little rye bread flavor

We LOVED this dish. I was looking for an authentic recipe after having cabbage served this way at a German restaurant. The combination of the butter, vinegar and sugar make the dish great. I followed the recipe and the cooking time which seemed long but it really needed the hour to cook. I didn't have cloves but used a dash of cinnamon instead. I read that cinnamon or allspice can be used as a substitute for cloves.
Delicious! Didn't know red cabbage could taste so good. I will cut the sugar by half next time and perhaps use an additional apple to make it a bit healthier.

They recently stopped selling my favorite jarred red cabbage in my local grocery store so I made this recipe instead of driving the 20 miles to the only store in my area for the jarred kind. I used some cheesecloth to make a satchel and put the apple and 2-3 whole cloves in it instead of using the ground clove. After simmering I removed the satchel so that I didn't have the apple and cloves in the finished product but still had their flavor in it. It was AMAZING and just as good if not better than the already prepared and jarred red cabbage! I will be using this from now on to top my potato pancakes (in addition to sour cream of course)!
I made this and it was tasty. I did sub caraway for the cloves, my personal preference. Although my children did not appreciate the smell while it was cooking!

This took me straight back to Germany. I took some snippets of advice from other reviewers: Brown sugar instead of white - about 3 tablespoons, 1/3 of a very large red onion (mostly just to use it up), about half the cloves (personal preference), 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon, about 1/4 cup apple cider vinegar (again, personal preference). 1/2 tsp salt. As you can see, this recipe has a great deal of versatility, so customize to your liking. So, so, so delicious. Herzlichen Dank für das leckere Rezept!

easy and yummy--hubby was suspicious but after one bite was a huge fan, and my toddler daughter loved it!
I made one substitution---used dark brown sugar instead of white sugar.
Also, I cooked in the crockpot on low for 6 hours...this will be a Winter staple in our house- thanks!

My Great Grandma from Germany made this every holiday. I fry up 4 strips of bacon and use the grease instead of butter to cook the cabbage, apple and spices in. Then I crumble the bacon and sprinkle it on top in the serving dish. I also use 4-5 whole cloves and 4-5 black pepper corns instead of the ground cloves and pepper. My whole house smells like childhood right now as it is cooking...love it!

I stayed pretty true to the ingredients except for drastically reducing the salt. Just guessing - I probably used 1/2 to 1 tsp total. I did it in the Instant Pot. I melted the butter, added the rest of the ingredients and stirred to mix, then put it on Steam for 15 min, did a quick pressure release when done. I stirred and did final check for seasoning, then served it.

I made this exactly as written with the exception of using nutmeg instead of cloves (hate 'em). This had a delicious flavor. I have to mention it was done in one hour. I found the Granny Smith apples to be overcooked (mush). I cut them as pictured in the directional photo. Next time I may let the cabbage cook some before adding the apples and see if that is an improvement. Overall, a good red cabbage recipe.

I make this a few times a year and my German dad loves it. The only change I’ve made is using white vinegar instead of Apple cider vinegar. I have tried it with both and just prefer the white vinegar. Sometimes I add bacon if I have some on hand (only because this is how I grew up eating it).

This was very good. The three Tbs. Water is unnecessary though as the cabbage releases lots of water when cooked. My personal preference was to use less sugar and more butter but that’s just for my taste. It’s a very easy and tasty recipe that I will make again.
It’s a great side dish or snack
Absolute perfection! And so easy!! My German grandma would love this recipe (if she wasn’t already using it!).
I've tried a lot of recipes but most are two sweet. This has the best balance of sweet and sour. It's my go to recipe.
I made it in the instapot. All the ingredients in the pot. Cook for 4 minutes and quick release. Cabbage perfect texture
It was better than expected. Will definitely make again
Excellent red cabbage recipe ! Couldn’t be easier and super tasty too
Made this for the first time for a church luncheon and it was a hit. I had people asking for the recipe. I was so amazed at how easy it is to make.
